text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on February 4 in history.
211 - Lucius Septimius Severus, Roman emperor responsible for making the empire's government a military monarchy, died.
1615 - Giovanni Battista della Porta, Italian physicist, philosopher and writer on the properties of lenses, died.
1746 - Tadeusz Andrezei Bonawentura Kosciuszko, Polish soldier and patriot, born. As well as battling the Russians at home, he fought in the American War of Independence.
1787 - Shays's Rebellion, an uprising of Massachusetts farmers led by Daniel Shays, ended with defeat at Petersham.
1789 - Presidential electors met and chose George Washington as America's first president.
1874 - The Battle of Kumasi ended the Ashanti War between Britain and Ghana.
1881 - Fernand Leger, French painter, born; he was noted for his "machine art" based on modern technology.
1897 - Ludwig Erhard, German economist and politician, born. He was the main architect of Germany's post-World War Two economic recovery, and was Chancellor from 1963 to 1966.
1902 - Charles Lindbergh, U.S. aviator and the first person to make a solo flight across the Atlantic in May 1937, born.
1904 - The Russo-Japanese war began when Japan laid siege to Port Arthur.
1906 - Dietrich Bonhoeffer, German theologian, philosopher and prominent anti-Nazi, born; he was executed in Flossenberg concentration camp for his part in the failed plot to assassinate Hitler.
1918 - Ida Lupino, British film actress, noted for her roles in "High Sierra" and "The Hitch-hiker", born.
1924 - Mahatma Gandhi was released after spending two years in jail in Bombay.
1927 - British driver Malcolm Campbell broke the world land speed record in his car Bluebird, driving at 174.224 miles per hour.
1938 - Adolf Hitler became Germany's War Minister and Joachim von Ribbentrop took over foreign affairs.
1945 - Winston Churchill, Franklin Roosevelt and Joseph Stalin met at Yalta in the Crimea to discuss plans for the defeat of the Axis powers and to decide on the post-war future.
1948 - Ceylon became a self-governing independent state within the Commonwealth.
1966 - An All Nippon Airways Boeing 727 jet aircraft crashed in Tokyo Bay. 133 passengers and crew were killed.
1971 - British carmaker Rolls Royce declared itself bankrupt.
1972 - Zambian President Kenneth Kuanda banned the opposition United Progressive Party and arrested its leader Simon Kapepwe together with over 120 members.
1974 - Patricia Hearst, grand-daughter of the late William Randolph Hearst, was kidnapped by the Symbionese Liberation Army.
1974 - Grenada achieved independence within the British Commonwealth.
1976 - An earthquake measuring 7.5 on the Richter scale and resulting mudslides caused the deaths of 23,000 people just north of Guatemala city; 1.5 million people were made homeless.
1976 - In Mozambique, the capital Lourenco Marques was renamed Maputo.
1978 - Junius Jayawardene was sworn in as Sri Lanka's first president.
1982 - In Britain, Laker Airways, pioneer of cheap transatlantic air fares, collapsed.
1987 - Liberace, U.S. pianist and showman, died.
1992 - Loyal troops put down an attempted coup against President Carlos Andres Perez in Venezuela.
1994 - Mortar bombs killed nine people in a food queue in Serb-besieged Sarajevo.
1994 - Polish Finance Minister Marek Borowski resigned after clashing with Prime Minister Waldemar Pawlak.
1996 - A Colombian cargo plane crashed into homes near the Paraguayan capital Asuncion, killing at least 22 people.
